name: Jesse
overview: Jesse was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the father of David. His role as David's father places him in the direct lineage of significant biblical figures, highlighting his importance in the ancestral line. No additional notes are provided about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Jesse appears only once in the record without any specific meaning or divine origin noted. It is presented simply as a proper name without further etymological detail.
familyAndRelationships: Jesse is explicitly identified as the father of David and Nethanel, Raddai, and Ozem. He is also inferred to be the father of Obed, Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah. These relationships establish Jesse as the patriarch of a notable family within the tribe of Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Jesse's significance in Scripture centers on his role as the father of David, a key figure in Israel's history and God's redemptive plan. Through Jesse's lineage, the promise to the tribe of Judah is fulfilled, culminating in the Davidic line from which the Messiah would come. Thus, Jesse serves as a vital link in the biblical genealogy that underscores God's sovereign work in salvation history.
